# We are doing
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(here)
library(readr)
library(patchwork)
library(car)
```


```{r}
# first step of the process
# raw data file
raw_data <- read_xlsx(here("pone.0302604.s004.xlsx"), skip = 1)
view(raw_data)
```


```{r}
# an R-squared of 0.7347 for 36 predictors 
overfitted_model <- lm(burnout ~., data = raw_data)
summary(overfitted_model)$r.squared

variance_inflation_factors <- tibble(
  variables = character(36),
  values = numeric(36)
)
for (i in 1:36) {
  variance_inflation_factors$values[i] <- vif(overfitted_model)[[i]]
  variance_inflation_factors$variables[i] <- names(vif(overfitted_model))[[i]]
}

variance_inflation_factors <- variance_inflation_factors %>%
  mutate(VIF_range = ifelse(values > 4, "4-5", ifelse(values < 4 & values > 3, "3-4", ifelse(values < 3 & values > 2, "2-3", ifelse(values < 2 & values > 1, "1-2", "less than 1")))))

variance_inflation_factors %>%
  arrange(desc(values))

ggplot(variance_inflation_factors, aes(x = VIF_range, color = VIF_range)) + geom_bar() + scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(4,5,12,15)) + labs(title = str_wrap("Binned Variance Inflation Factors for predicting burnout with all variables in the 'raw data'", width = 45), x = "VIF range", legend = "VIF range")
```

```{r}
# fitting a model with the variance inflation factors restricted from 1-3
variance_inflation_factors_reduced <- variance_inflation_factors %>%
  filter(VIF_range %in% c("1-2", "2-3"))
raw_data_reduced <- raw_data %>% select(variance_inflation_factors_reduced$variables, burnout)

lm.reduced <- lm(burnout ~., data = raw_data_reduced)

summary(lm.reduced)$r.squared

# this model has 20 predictors, and the variables with the higher-end of
# the variance inflation factors have been removed

vif(lm.reduced)
```

```{r}
summary(lm.reduced)
```

If we take the predictors that are considered to be significant under the standard 0.05 threshold with the model that only contains the variables with variance inflation factors less than 3 from the original 36 predictor model, then we would fit a model on 'physical', 'meaning purpose', 'apathetic', and motivated'

```{r}
# to be clear, this model takes the significant predictors (p>0.05) for the model
# of reduced variance inflation (cutting the 3+ threshold) from the 36 
# predictor model
lm.reduced.sig <- lm(burnout ~ physical + meaning_purpose + apathetic, data = raw_data_reduced)
summary(lm.reduced.sig)$r.squared
```


```{r}

# these variables are those that were listed to be 'statistically significant' from the model that they fit, where their p-values for the t-test for each variable
# was less than .05

fitted_variables <- raw_data %>% select(burnout,apathetic, self_compassion, compassion_fatigue, mental_wellbeing,depression,receptive,connectedness, worry, dissociation, perception)

# fitting a regression model from which the R^2 values were obtained

fitted.lm <- lm(burnout ~., data = fitted_variables)

summary(fitted.lm)$r.squared

sig_variables <- raw_data %>% select(burnout,apathetic, self_compassion, compassion_fatigue, mental_wellbeing,depression,receptive,connectedness)
```


Looking at the original paper

* The **burnout variable** is considered to be the response variable
* their first multiple linear regression model is fit using the variables that have p-values under 0.05 for t-tests regarding whether the value of the coefficient is non-zero or not
  - these people do not seem to be treating the 0.05 significance level like a 'night' and 'day' thing
  
* they use the variables *apathetic*, *self compassion*, *compassion fatigue*, *mental wellbeing*, *depression*, *receptive*, and *connectedness*
* the $R^2$ in their model is 0.70, and they say that 70% of the variation in burnout scores is explained by the regressors, but again, this does not tell us anything about the appropriateness of the model fit.
  - a good question to address is whether they are still overfitting their regression model after removing the non-significant predictors--worry, dissociation, and perception--
  
  The predictor variables are:
* burnout 
* apathetic
* compassion_fatigue
* mental_wellbeing
* depression
* receptive
* connectedness


* removed variables that are not considered to be 'statistically significant'
  - this includes 'worry,' 'dissociation,', and 'perception'
  - the authors of the article mentioned that the predictors explain about 70% of the variation in burnout (when including the 'non-statistically significant' predictors)

```{r}
# manually creating their "S1 Table" for the number of online diary entries for each month

Number.of.entries <- c(23,9,24,12,22,17,13,16,12,15,7,8,6,6,5,15,9)

S1.Table <- data.frame(Months, Number.of.entries)
```
